selection: first qualifying samples in native traversal order; at most three removed-row and three retained-clipping/visibility cases, with unique photographs across both groups

panels_reviewed.observation: Bottom-edge targets move outside the augmented canvas; retained partial boxes follow the remaining image extent.
Upper-edge fronts are cropped, with observed lower-corner dots retained on their transformed physical landmarks.
Upper-edge fronts are clipped; known corner dots remain attached to the transformed visible landmarks.
An upper-edge source target moves outside the canvas; the neighboring retained target is clipped at the upper boundary.
An upper-edge target is clipped after the native transform; known corner dots stay on the surviving physical lower edge.
Bottom-edge targets move outside the canvas; one removed target retains a subpixel box sliver, and the retained partial target is clipped at the bottom.

decision: Retain current augmentation policy; the sampled removals and corner-availability transitions do not demonstrate inconsistent supervision.
limitations: Six deterministically selected panels were visually inspected, not every transformed object contour.
Box clipping and area ratios are geometric measurements, not physical segmentation or recognizability measurements.
Frozen source annotations were not independently re-adjudicated by this audit.
The diagnostic does not train or score a model and cannot establish whether changing augmentation improves recognition.
